title: Large Language Models are overconfident and amplify human bias

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting LLMs with algorithmically generated YES/NO reasoning questions with known ground truths, eliciting self-reported confidence probabilities, and calculating the bias as the difference between the self-reported confidence and the actual accuracy rate. This is also compared against a human baseline.

Comparing an LLM's direct self-reported overall confidence with a derived confidence measure (calculated by multiplying the model's self-reported confidence in its 'facts' and its 'reasoning') to evaluate internal consistency and the presence of conjunction fallacies in self-assessment.

Analyzing demographic differences in human experiments to evaluate the baseline overconfidence gap between male and female participants, as well as their differing changes in confidence and accuracy after exposure to LLM assistance.
